name: Gandhian socialism
summary: Gandhian socialism is the social and economic outlook drawn from Mahatma Gandhi: an ethical, nonviolent socialism of sarvodaya (the welfare of all), trusteeship of wealth, decentralised self-sufficient villages and bread labour. It seeks economic equality by conversion and constructive work rather than class war or state ownership, distrusts industrial civilization and centralised power, and treats politics as inseparable from religion and truth.
scope: Gandhi's own thought (Hind Swaraj 1909, the Constructive Programme, his trusteeship writings in Harijan) as continued by the Sarvodaya movement under Vinoba Bhave. It excludes the 1980s BJP slogan of the same name, which the catalog's suggested Wikipedia article treats as a Hindu nationalist variant, and it excludes Marxist and parliamentary socialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Adherents split: Hind Swaraj calls hospitals and modern medicine corrupting, yet the creed's concern for the poorest suggests public provision; the question is never addressed directly, so this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Gandhi's trusteeship formula calls for a minimum living wage alongside a maximum income, with the gap narrowing over time.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Gandhian economics subordinates economics to ethics and rejects the self-maximising market actor, favouring small local production over price-driven allocation; Gandhi also did not advocate full state planning, hence only -1.

public-ownership.rationale: The Constructive Programme says heavy industries will need to be centralized and nationalized, while most activity stays in villages; Gandhi disliked railways, so support is moderate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He called for levelling down the few rich and allowed legislative regulation of wealth, though he preferred voluntary trusteeship to compulsion.

unions-good.rationale: The Constructive Programme calls the nonviolent Ahmedabad Labour Union a model for all India to copy, praising unions built on nonviolence and arbitration.

property-fundamental.rationale: Trusteeship, quoted from Harijan, does not recognize any right of private ownership except as society permits, so property is a conditional trust rather than a fundamental right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: State-regulated trusteeship and the statement that trusteeship does not exclude legislative regulation of ownership and use of wealth imply tighter rules on business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: bread labour and self-reliance cut against passive dependency, but the creed's priority for the poor makes cutting welfare unattractive; Gandhi did not address welfare programs as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Gandhi held that labour power is the worker's own property, but his remedy was trusteeship by owners and village cooperation, not collective worker ownership of firms; adherents differ, so inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's insistence on openness and fearlessness (students do nothing in secret) and distrust of state power; terrorism-era surveillance is anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The Constructive Programme makes prohibition a vital moral reform and speaks of the curse of intoxicants and narcotics.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred and split: nonviolence and communal unity oppose hatred, but Gandhi's reliance on persuasion and civil liberties for dissent does not clearly favour legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Gandhi's ideal was power flowing down to the individual and the people, with parliaments deriving authority from them; a leader bypassing institutions runs against that, though he valued moral leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Gandhi called himself a philosophical anarchist with an ideal of ordered anarchy, yet he accepted nationalised heavy industry and a regulating state in practice; adherents split between ideal and practice.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred and split: nonviolence opposes arms, but Gandhi objected to colonial disarmament of Indians; no direct statement was found.

empower-police-military.rationale: Hind Swaraj holds the sword useless for holding India and the Constructive Programme builds a nonviolent order, so more armed authority is rejected.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's emphasis on self-restraint, purity and women's dignity; sex work is not discussed in the sources read.

decide-locally.rationale: Khadi mentality means decentralization of production and distribution, with every village producing its necessaries, and independence is said to belong to every unit down to the humblest.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and the conversion of wrongdoers rather than vengeance; penal policy is not addressed in the sources read.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: Gandhi valued family and village life but demanded radical change in women's status (wives as comrades, not dolls), so support is qualified.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's emphasis on traditional morals and self-restraint; the issue is anachronistic and not addressed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from ahimsa and reverence for life; the question is not discussed in the sources read.

more-religion-public.rationale: Gandhian thought sees little line between sacred and social and calls modern civilization irreligion, wanting politics informed by religious ethics, though non-sectarian.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the programme to end untouchability and its demand for independence without distinction of race, colour or creed; the question concerns racial rather than caste injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gandhi said women's subordination was made by custom and law shaped by men, but he also held distinct roles of service; adherents split, and the framing is anachronistic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Swadeshi, khadi and the love of the mother tongue over English express a commitment to preserving indigenous culture and economy, though Gandhi's idea was inclusive.

gradual-change.rationale: Gandhi urged constructive work and slow conversion, but also a revolutionary change of mentality now and said equality's foundations must be laid before swaraj; adherents split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive nationhood suggests no hostility, while village self-sufficiency suggests no strong view either, so neutral by inference.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Constructive Programme calls independence compatible with interdependence, but no position on international bodies is stated; inferred neutral.

free-trade.rationale: Swadeshi, the boycott of foreign goods and the call to use village products rather than foreign or machine-made ones put self-sufficiency over free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Gandhi said independence is never exclusive and is compatible with interdependence, rejecting aggressive nationalism, though swadeshi favours the home economy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Soul-force is set against brute force and the sword is called useless, so military intervention is rejected even for humanitarian aims.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; universalist outlook and local rootedness pull in opposite directions, so inferred neutral.

limit-growth.rationale: Gandhian economics aims to meet needs rather than multiply wants and treats endless growth in material wants as harmful.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the creed's restraint, decentralisation and critique of industrial civilization; climate change itself was not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Hind Swaraj treats modern civilization as a moral sickness and technology as aggravating it, though Gandhi welcomed labour-saving tools such as the sewing machine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from distrust of large centralised technology and from nonviolence; nuclear power is anachronistic for the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Gandhi warned a violent and bloody revolution was coming unless the rich shared voluntarily and said the violent way has never succeeded; he sought change through nonviolent conversion, not revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hind Swaraj attacks lawyers and doctors as self-serving professions and the programme puts power in the people and the village rather than in specialists.

central-planning.rationale: Economic life is to be decentralised into self-sufficient villages, though the programme does allow nationalized heavy industry; central planning of the whole economy is not the model.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: village cooperative production and trusteeship suggest acceptance of local exchange under communal ownership; Gandhi never discussed market socialism by name.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; trusteeship justifies community claims on wealth, but a single land tax is not mentioned.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: wealth from legacy is said to be held for the community beyond an honourable livelihood, but no inheritance tax is stated.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: bread labour and the dignity of work make an unconditional payment unattractive; Gandhi stressed work for all, not transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Swadeshi and the call to use village products to the exclusion of foreign goods favour protecting indigenous production.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Heavy industry is to be nationalized but most activity is to be village-based and voluntary; directing investment to strategic industries is not discussed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Production is to be spread across villages and families, each growing and making for its own needs, which favours wide small-scale holding over concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: trusteeship keeps a minimum living wage and maximum income, so wages persist in the transition; abolition is not proposed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; inferred neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: Gandhi favoured voluntary arbitration in the Ahmedabad union rather than state-recognised bodies that fix wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Constructive Programme says power resides in the people, not in assemblies or ruling bodies, and Gandhi sought a nonviolent order of self-governing units, ruling out single-party guidance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from the call that rulers and princes become trustees and from swaraj as self-rule; no direct statement on monarchy as an institution.

democracy-best.rationale: Gandhi called democracy the settling of disputes without violence, but Hind Swaraj mocks parliament as a costly toy and he favoured village self-rule; qualified, inferred support.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the preference for village self-governance and Panchayat-style direct deliberation; referendums are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; decentralised self-rule is compatible but Gandhi never proposed councils as the basis of political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Gandhi stressed the independence of every unit but opposed partition; no clear position on secession, so inferred neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: The aim of power moving down to the individual and sarvodaya, the welfare of all, rejects a ruling class by nature.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hind Swaraj and the Constructive Programme reject violence, including assassination, and say the violent way to change has never succeeded.

war-builds-character.rationale: Soul-force is set against brute force, and Gandhi rejected war as a school of virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents give equal respect to all religions but do not want religion walled off from public life; inferred from the sacred-and-social unity.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hind Swaraj treats religions as converging roads and insists on equal respect for all, so one scripture should not supply the state's laws.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: Gandhi condemned lawyers and the court system and distrusted violence, so private courts and private defence are unlikely to appeal.

military-superiority.rationale: Nonviolence and the rejection of the sword lead adherents to reject a drive for military superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hind Swaraj says India cannot cease to be one nation because people of different religions live in it, rejecting an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Gandhi framed the choice as voluntary sharing or a violent revolution and sought to abolish the conflict of capital and labour, not treat it as history's engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Economic equality is the master key to nonviolent independence, with a levelling down of the rich and levelling up of the poor and a narrowing income gap.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the programme's service to adivasis and the principle of independence for every unit; no direct statement on land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Gandhi condemned colonial exploitation but did not discuss reparations; inferred neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from the focus on a single Indian nation across religions and nonviolent internationalism; no political union of civilizations is advocated.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Gandhian economics rejects the picture of humans as rational maximisers and aims at sarvodaya, the welfare of all against the welfare of a few.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Hind Swaraj defines civilization as conduct that shows the path of duty, and trusteeship casts ownership as a duty of stewardship.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from ahimsa and the programme's concern for cattle and village sanitation; no explicit statement on intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; Gandhi favoured self-control, not state limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Hind Swaraj calls modern civilization irreligion, but Gandhi's 1921 foreword says he did not aim to destroy railways or hospitals, so the strong form is tempered.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Hind Swaraj and the preference for labour-using, local technology reject accelerating disruptive technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the critique of modern technology and the emphasis on self-discipline over technical remedies.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from decentralised, person-centred self-rule; anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; inferred neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hind Swaraj idealises the old village order, yet Gandhi demanded radical reform such as ending untouchability; adherents split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hind Swaraj says means are like a seed and ends like a tree, so policy cannot be judged by results alone.

direct-action.rationale: The Constructive Programme calls civil disobedience the storehouse of power and denies that power comes only through legislative assemblies, though nonviolence is required.

means-match-ends.rationale: Hind Swaraj compares means to a seed and ends to a tree, and the Constructive Programme builds the nonviolent society through nonviolent daily work.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ideal is settled self-sufficient villages growing cotton and food, not foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gandhi urged the union of intelligence and manual labour, and bread labour for all, but kept village crafts and specialisation; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Gandhian economics aims at needs rather than wants and surplus beyond need is held in trust for the poorest.

production-for-use.rationale: Each village is to produce all its necessaries first, and the economy is aimed at meeting needs rather than multiplying wants.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Gandhi wished to end capitalism almost as much as socialists but sought to reform owners as trustees and did not analyse profit as exploitation; adherents split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class, imposed by force, contradicts nonviolent independence and the equal power of rich and poor.

collective-farming.rationale: Gandhi favoured village cooperation and later Gramdan, but Constructive Programme farming is by families on their own plots; inferred neutral.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Gandhi said nonviolent government is impossible amid large inequalities but made no such claim about imperial wars; inferred neutral.

taxation-theft.rationale: Trusteeship allows legislative regulation of wealth and the Constructive Programme demands levelling the rich, so taxation is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: The Constructive Programme backs prohibition of intoxicants, which restricts adults for their own sake.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred from the stress on duty, the village and the independence of every unit rather than individual rights alone.

conscription.rationale: Compelling military service conflicts with nonviolence and soul-force.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: the creed prizes participation in self-governing communities rather than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Gandhian economics subordinates economics to ethics and rejects treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Constructive Programme says political freedom has been won but economic freedom remains to be won, implying freedom needs material means.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Gandhi demanded independence and equal standing without distinction of race, colour or creed, which rejects racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from village self-governance (Panchayat Raj) building up from local bodies; guild representation is not addressed.

total-state.rationale: Gandhi's ideal was ordered anarchy and power resting with individuals, the opposite of a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Gandhi spoke of moral and social renewal through the constructive programme but not of a radical national rebirth from decadence; inferred neutral.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nonviolence and the rejection of conquest rule out expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from rejection of hierarchy in favour of self-rule.

bound-labor.rationale: The programme insists on the dignity of the kisans and the equality of workers, so bondage to a lord is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hind Swaraj criticises modern science and professions as products of a civilization, but this stops short of a general thesis about knowledge and power; inferred neutral.

universal-morality.rationale: Hind Swaraj and Gandhi's idea of truth treat religions as roads converging on one underlying truth and a common duty.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred from sarvodaya, welfare of all, and decision by conversion and consensus; the contrast with interest-balancing is not stated.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's religious universalism and objection to nations defined by religion; the question is not covered in the sources read.

revive-national-language.rationale: The programme urges Hindustani as common language and condemns love of English over mother tongues; revival of a dead language is not discussed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the dignity of labour and the idea that the worker owns labour power; no direct statement on democratic firm governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: Gandhi's education plan (Nai Talim) was community-based and crafts-centred rather than market-driven.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Constructive Programme ties political freedom to economic freedom, though Gandhi meant economic equality, not laissez-faire.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gandhi's method relies on moral example, with moneyed Congressmen told to lead the way, and on ordered anarchy with minimal enforcement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Poorna Swaraj is defined as the independence of every unit of the nation without distinction of race, colour or creed.

force-without-un.rationale: Rejecting force as such, adherents oppose its use abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Gandhi grounded politics in religion and conscience, not reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the universalist concern of sarvodaya for all; no direct statement.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from bread labour, the duty of all to do some manual work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Trusteeship and the Ahmedabad union aimed to abolish the conflict between capital and labour through cooperation rather than class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from reverence for national culture and non-destruction; the idea is not addressed.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed in class terms; inferred neutral.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme says women have as much right to shape their destiny as men and the legal status of women demands radical alteration.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; inferred neutral.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Independence without distinction of race and the attack on untouchability reject legally enforced separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Gandhi viewed the state as coercive but did not adopt a class-instrument theory; inferred neutral.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the critique of industrial growth and local energy self-sufficiency; anachronistic.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from respect for all cultures and religions; immigration is not discussed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of communal suspicion and conspiracy; not directly addressed.

national-mission.rationale: Gandhi hoped India would present nonviolence to the world but did not frame a mission to spread a government form; inferred neutral.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The programme says women were suppressed by custom and law made by men, which points the same way, though the sociological claim is modern.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hind Swaraj calls parliament a costly toy driven by party interest, and the programme warns of moneyed leaders; stated loosely, so low.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive eugenics conflicts with nonviolence and equal worth.

night-watchman-state.rationale: State-regulated trusteeship and the demand for economic equality require more than a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Independence without distinction of race and the rejection of untouchability oppose discouraging marriage across lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme calls untouchability a blot and curse on Hinduism and grounds swaraj on equality without distinction of race, colour or creed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; inferred neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Gandhi criticised proselytising but did not clearly back legal bans; inferred neutral.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Gandhi valued cow service (improvement of cattle) but opposed forcing it on other communities; adherents split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Gandhi's ideal of ordered anarchy and a diminishing state contradicts a state growing stronger indefinitely.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Hind Swaraj says the English hold India because Indians cooperate, and the Constructive Programme says power resides in the people and is only entrusted to representatives.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from swadeshi self-sufficiency rather than export-led growth.

population-transfer.rationale: Communal unity and independence without distinction of creed exclude expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonviolence is the core of the creed and bars violence against persons.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Gandhian economics values cooperation and sarvodaya over struggle between individuals and peoples.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from swaraj as self-rule and the demand that the poor enjoy equal power with the rich.

vanguard-party.rationale: The programme says power resides in the people and kisans organised on their own felt grievances, and refuses power politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme demands levelling up the semi-starved millions and Gandhian economics holds surplus in trust for the poorest.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Gandhi favoured nonviolent strikes (Ahmedabad) under arbitration but not legal restriction; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Gandhi blamed the destruction of village industry and inequality for poverty rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hind Swaraj argues India is one nation across religions and that disputes were stirred by outsiders.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and truthful means.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from the insistence on transparency (nothing done in secret) and self-rule.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and the rejection of party rule.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from simple living and the contrast of palaces with poor hovels.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the stress on conscience and the critique of party interest in parliament.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Interdependence is accepted but supranational unions are not discussed; inferred neutral.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of concentrated power.

clerical-rule.rationale: Equal respect for all religions rules out rule by one faith's scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Gandhi urged noncooperation with war but not a strategy of defeating one's own government; inferred neutral.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from moral reformism balanced by reliance on persuasion.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the principle that power belongs to the people and is entrusted to representatives.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of militarism.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for gradual, voluntary change.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Hind Swaraj prefers small villages to cities and the programme places most national activity in the villages.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Gandhi opposed the partition of India, but the general question is not addressed.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The programme blames a love of English and the divorce of intelligence from labour for a chasm between educated classes and the masses.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hind Swaraj ranks modern civilization below the ancient Indian one while insisting on equal religions; adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence; capital punishment is not discussed in the sources read.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from moral reform and self-restraint.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the inclusive idea of the nation.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme values the mother tongues and Hindustani in both scripts; minority language policy is not stated.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Constructive Programme says Congress has won political freedom but must still win economic freedom, and links complete independence to economic equality.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; inferred neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Truth and nonviolent means reject sacrificing freedom for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Gandhi stressed self-reliance but also sharing; the question is not addressed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nonviolence rejects nuclear and other armaments.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the preference for peace over claims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Trusteeship states that wealth belongs to the community beyond an honourable livelihood and ownership is permitted only as society allows.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from restraint and critique of heedless industrialisation.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of military alliances; not addressed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from religion's close tie to social life; no direct statement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence even though Gandhi opposed partition.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the independence of every unit.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Ordered anarchy and power rooted in the people exclude sacralised rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Levelling down the rich requires progressive burdens.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Power is entrusted by the people and held in trust, so rulers are bound.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from limited wants and the critique of material ambition.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's emphasis on power in the people and humility; not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Trusteeship asked zamindars to outgrow greed rather than be dispossessed, and Gandhi relied on voluntary sharing.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the inclusive nation and nonviolence.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hind Swaraj respects all religions as roads to one truth, so punishing leaving one is excluded.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the programme's call to end women's suppression by custom and law.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the inclusive nation and local self-rule.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from independence of every unit.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Gandhi's South African experience and Hind Swaraj favour equal rights where one lives; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Gandhian economics makes economics a servant of ethics, rejecting an economic engine of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the levelling down of concentrated wealth.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from distrust of majoritarian parliaments.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women as equal partners but parity quotas not addressed; inferred neutral.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Swadeshi favours self-sufficiency, but Gandhi explicitly accepted interdependence and rejected exclusion.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the ethical subordination of economics.

moral-incentives.rationale: Gandhian economics rests on service, bread labour and ethics rather than material incentive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Violence is rejected and the sword called useless.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme condemns untouchability and the ruling classes are urged to give up privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on Indian civilization.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hind Swaraj rejects British rule's claim to civilise and demands self-rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Student rules include the tricolour and loyalty, but no statement on teaching pride; inferred neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Gandhi hoped capitalism could reform itself through trusteeship but is not clear on collapse; inferred neutral.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of domination.

delink-world-market.rationale: Swadeshi leans toward delinking but interdependence is accepted; inferred neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The programme condemns untouchability and discrimination as a blot and curse.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from power entrusted by the people to chosen representatives.

minority-veto.rationale: Gandhi valued consensus and conscience but did not set an unlimited veto; inferred neutral.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Civil disobedience is said to be the storehouse of power, though nonviolent; removal is not specified.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Hind Swaraj mocks Parliament as a costly toy and the programme says power resides in the people.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from ahimsa and the programme's cow service and improvement of cattle.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Gandhian ahimsa leans against animal use, but humane use is not discussed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Trusteeship states directly that the wealthy hold their wealth in trust for the community and the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Constructive Programme demands active constructive work for swaraj from everyone.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hind Swaraj says the English hold India through Indian cooperation, so rule depends on consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The programme speaks of the wanton destruction of village industry; a world-system theory is not stated.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Swadeshi and village self-sufficiency put reliance on one's own resources first.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Hind Swaraj rejects copying English institutions: swaraj is not English rule without Englishmen.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nonviolence and power in the people exclude a guardian army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the dignity of labour and women's service.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from duty and traditional ethics.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from power entrusted to representatives by the people.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of financialised self-interest.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Trusteeship allows private ownership only as society permits, which suggests tenure conditional on community use.

single-official-language.rationale: The programme wants Hindustani as common language alongside mother tongues; not a sole official language.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Gandhian economics aims to meet needs rather than multiply wants.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from trusteeship and the call for state regulation of wealth.

job-guarantee.rationale: Production is meant to spread employment widely; no state guarantee is stated.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Gandhi disobeyed unjust laws but valued voluntary obedience of just ones; adherents split.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from respect for national self-rule.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hind Swaraj says disputes between communities were stirred by outsiders and communal unity is essential.

local-production.rationale: The Constructive Programme says every village should produce all its necessaries and a surplus for city needs.

religious-nation.rationale: Hind Swaraj says India is one nation regardless of religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Hind Swaraj rejects submission to a dominant power.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Gandhi taught non-possession and trust, so private belongings are not a clear issue; inferred neutral.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence; communism is rejected as violent but not to be defeated.

religion-illusion.rationale: Gandhian economics aims at spiritual development.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Hind Swaraj sees modern industrial civilization as a moral illness.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from family-based service; not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Hindustani is to take both Hindi and Urdu forms, so purism is rejected.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The creed envisions small self-sufficient cooperative villages.

majority-settlement.rationale: Communal unity and equality rule out engineering settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Trusteeship is offered as a third course between capitalism and violent socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and inclusive nationhood.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nonviolent truth-seeking and power in the people exclude suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Equal respect for religions excludes punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hind Swaraj is a sustained attack on foreign exploitation of India.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Violent removal and religious rule are both rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Village self-governance involves direct popular participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The programme links untouchability, women and economic injustice; not framed as intersectionality.

alienated-labor.rationale: The programme says the divorce between labour and intelligence has caused stagnation and the village's decline.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Hind Swaraj says Hindus and Muslims have lived together and must continue as one nation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Gandhi spoke of God as truth but locates power in people; adherents split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nonviolent independence implies no reliance on armed forces, though Gandhi accepted transitional needs.

rich-first.rationale: Gandhi demanded levelling now rather than letting some grow rich first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Power rooted in the people excludes hereditary rule.

property-franchise.rationale: The programme says the poor must enjoy the same power as the richest.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the concern about power of wealth.

racial-franchise.rationale: Independence without distinction of race is the stated aim.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Communal unity rules out communal boycotts.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Gandhi called untouchability a blot on Hinduism, reinterpreting practice against custom.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The programme says a nonviolent government is impossible while a wide gulf separates rich and hungry.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ordered anarchy is the ideal but practical; adherents split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Voluntary trusteeship is preferred to compulsion, though legislation is allowed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The programme says wives should be honoured comrades rather than dolls.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from rejection of military-style training.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from swaraj and rejection of domination.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The holder of wealth is entitled only to an honourable livelihood; labour power is the true property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence extends to refusing to kill even in defence, though he preferred courage with violence to cowardice.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Hind Swaraj traces India's unity to ancient pilgrimage ties.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Gandhian economics and politics are inseparable from ethics and spiritual aims.

culture-before-state.rationale: The programme builds swaraj from below through constructive work on mentality before state power.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the call to end women's suppression by custom and law.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Independence without distinction of creed rejects ethnic economic dominance.

independent-unions.rationale: The programme says labour must not be used for power politics.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from decentralisation and communal provision.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from community claims on wealth.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from village-based self-rule linking up.

family-wage.rationale: The trusteeship formula calls for a minimum living wage.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from critique of modern medicine.

person-over-state.rationale: The ideal is power moving down to the individual with self-rule replacing state enforcement.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Gandhian economics aims at spiritual development and refuses a purely material view.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the independence of every unit.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the critique of industrial agriculture.

dense-cities.rationale: Hind Swaraj prefers small villages to large cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Independence without racial distinction is the aim.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence; armed defence is accepted only as a lesser evil.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by shared life across religions, not language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Communal unity is the first item of the programme; separate electorates divide it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Hind Swaraj blames outsiders for stirring disputes, but no partition plot claim is stated.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the priority to the poor.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the programme's view of women's role in nonviolence.

arms-reduction.rationale: Hind Swaraj calls the sword useless and nonviolence the basis of peace.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Ahmedabad union settled disputes by arbitration.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the critique of exploitation.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Hind Swaraj rejects English rule without Englishmen, but Gandhi sought nonviolent change.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of treating the world as an economic resource.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The programme says village industry was destroyed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Hind Swaraj says religions are different roads converging on the same point.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from concern for farmers hurt by market swings.

workers-own-party.rationale: The programme says labour and kisans should not be used for power politics.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the call to end women's suppression.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The programme says the legal and customary status of women demands radical alteration.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The programme treats Hindi and Urdu as two forms of one language, Hindustani.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Hind Swaraj treats all religions as equal roads.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Gandhi saw democracy as nonviolent settlement of disputes, more than procedure.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme says women have as much right to shape their destiny as men.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Gandhi blamed custom and law rather than religion itself.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Trusteeship rejects absolute private claims to land.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from rejection of central planning.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from village self-government linking upward.

simple-living.rationale: Gandhian economics urges needs over wants and the programme's students are to live with self-restraint and village products.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Wealth beyond need belongs to the community.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from priority to the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from distrust of leader-centred power.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Communal unity is the first item of the programme.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The 1921 foreword accepts some modern tools while upholding old ideals; adherents split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Gandhi welcomed machines that reduce drudgery but opposed labour-displacing technology and wanted production decentralised and employing many; the statement reverses his proposal.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Trusteeship treats wealth as a trust held for society and aims at economic equality with income limits, so how wealth came about does not by itself make a distribution just.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from swadeshi and distrust of large-scale finance and industrial civilization that a levy on speculative cross-border finance would be welcomed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed for racial groups abroad; inferred from the Constructive Programme's insistence that untouchability and communal division remain central obstacles to equality.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Satyagraha rests on the duty to disobey laws that conflict with conscience and truth, accepting the penalty; Hind Swaraj says passive resisters need not obey unjust laws.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the ideal of self-governing villages in oceanic circles and distrust of centralised power, which favours many centres over one dominant power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Bread labour and the dignity of labour make labour the source of worth, but Gandhi gave no formal value theory, so this is inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Swadeshi and sarvodaya join love of country with service of the poorest villagers; Gandhi's patriotism was humane rather than exclusive.

material-over-identity.rationale: The Constructive Programme puts communal unity, removal of untouchability and women's equality beside economic work, and Gandhi stressed moral and spiritual ends over material interests alone.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Gandhian socialism rejects state ownership, class war and centralised party power in favour of decentralised village economy and voluntary trusteeship.

missingStatements.text: Everyone should do some manual labour to earn their own living.
missingStatements.rationale: Bread labour and the dignity of labour are central to Gandhian economics and the programme's union of intelligence and labour.
missingStatements.declined: Gandhian bread-labour is specific to this ideology; abolish-division-of-labor and simple-living cover the nearest contested ground.

missingStatements.text: Technology should be chosen to employ many people rather than to replace labour.
missingStatements.rationale: Gandhi welcomed machines that reduce drudgery but wanted technology that is labour-using, not labour-displacing, and production decentralised.

missingStatements.text: A legal maximum should be set on any person's income.
missingStatements.rationale: The trusteeship formula calls for a maximum income and a minimum living wage, narrowing the gap over time.

notes: The catalog's suggested Wikipedia article is about a Hindu-nationalist variant (BJP, 1980s); this profile represents Gandhi's own socialism and the Sarvodaya tradition. Most answers outside economics, violence and religion are inferred (low).
